key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening framework can rapidly identify phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites with strong optical properties by combining interpretable descriptors and DFT-validated inverse design.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical materials-discovery pipeline for safer semiconductors in photovoltaics, sensors, and transparent electronics, reducing the search from thousands of candidates to a handful of experimentally relevant compounds.
method: Trained ML surrogates on 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Used a recall-optimized stability classifier and an XGBoost band-gap regressor to rank charge-balanced lead-free compositions.
Applied staged inverse-design constraints to 13,088 candidates and validated the top hits with DFT and convex-hull stability checks.
evidence_signal: The stability classifier achieved ROC-AUC = 0.92 and the band-gap regressor achieved R2 = 0.93 on held-out data, and five final candidates were DFT-validated on the convex hull.
watch_item: The pipeline is promising but still depends on the quality and domain coverage of the DFT training set, so experimental validation and compositional generalization remain important.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
